contexts.text: It will burn even to the lowest Hell ().
Burning pitch () stands for direful cupidities.
(The Lord burned to save the human race.)
Anger is said relatively to evil; wrath, to falsity; and the burning heat of anger () to both.
The ardour of affection, Signified.
The continued ardour of conjunction, Signified.
Lo! the bush was burning with fire = that scientific truth was full of the good of Divine love.
The solar fire in the other life is fire of such ardour that... AC 6849.
To burn, to grow warm, fire of flame () stand for cupidities themselves.
Burning as a furnace () stands for the cupidities of evil.
They speak and preach from ardour as of zeal... but it is ardour from the fire of the love of self and of the world.
Divine Good itself is in itself a flame of infinite ardour; that is, of love...
The ardour of domineering and of getting rich...
Hence it is that anger is described in the Word by fire, and is said to burn. Illustrated.

The Divine Love... is most ardent, and... much more ardent (than the natural sun), wherefore the Lord as a Sun does not flow in immediately into the Heavens, but the ardour of His love is tempered on the way by means of degrees... TCR 691.
From infernal ardour he torments those who do not worship him as a deity...
As it were a mountain burning with fire... = the appearance of infernal love.

There fell from Heaven a great star burning as it were a lamp = the appearance of Own intelligence from pride arising from infernal love... By a star, and also by a lamp, is signified intelligence; here, Own intelligence, because it was seen to burn, and all Own intelligence burns from pride, and the pride of it arises from infernal love, which is signified by a burning mountain.
A zeal which is outwardly sharp, harsh, burning...
That smoke, when kindled, burned as a flame...
The Angels... are burning to know...
As God, from His essence, burned with the love of uniting Himself with man...
(The use of the word burn, Illustrated.)
To burn as a lamp = to be falsified from Own love; to burn is said of Own love, because fire signifies it.
